Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The players and the umpires have made their way out in the middle. Tadiwanashe Marumani and Craig Ervine are the openers for Zimbabwe. Harry Tector comes to bowl. Here we go...
... The Run Chase ...

Zimbabwe were excellent with the ball! It was Ryan Burl who ran havoc and provided a great spell for his team. He ended with three wickets beside his name. Wellington Masakadza was very economical and bagged two wickets as well. Richard Ngarava and Chatara took two wickets too, whilst Evans has one in his kitty. Zimbabwe will be counting on their batters now to chase this low score down with ease. Which team will get over the line? To find out, do join us for the second essay in a short while.

Ireland have struggled with the blade here and they kept on losing wickets at regular intervals. Stephan Doheny and Curtis Campher were the only two batters from the top order who scored in double digits. The rest of the batters kept on giving their wickets away, with no one trying to just consolidate. Gareth Delany played a good knock at the end and scored 24 runs off 20 deliveries and has given the Irish bowlers a fighting chance in the game.

A dull outing for the visitors and Zimbabwe will be pleased with how things have panned out at the halfway mark. They have outclassed the visitors with the ball and would be the happier side going into the break as they have kept Ireland to a below-par score of 114 runs.

OUT! TAKEN! A spectacular catch from Craig Ervine and Ireland have been bundled out here! Tendai Chatara pitches it up outside off. Barry McCarthy hangs deep in his crease and looks to loft it over mid off. The timing isn't great but still, the ball seems to go over mid off. Ervine over there takes a couple of steps back and jumps backward to take a one-handed stunner with his left hand. McCarthy cannot believe it and Ireland have been bowled out for 114!
Commentary.Howout: c Craig Ervine b Tendai Chatara

Commentary.Commentary: This is slower and shorter well outside the off stump. Barry McCarthy walks past the stumps and looks to pull but misses. No wide is called.
This is around middle and leg, Barry McCarthy pushes it back to the bowler who fumbles and the ball rolls toward mid on. They get the single.
LEG BYE! Slower one bowled into the pitch and around leg stump. Fionn Hand looks to pull but misses. The ball goes off his body and towards backward point. They scamper through for one.
Back of a length and outside off, Barry McCarthy makes room and cuts it toward deep point for a single.
FOUR! Excellent shot! Just a fraction shorter and outside off, Barry McCarthy cuts it hard and finds the point boundary. The fielder from deep cover couldn't get there as it was timed beautifully.
Good length around off, this is played square of the wicket on the off side for a couple of runs.
Barry McCarthy walks in.

OUT! CLEANED HIM UP! 'You miss, I hit,' stuff from Richard Ngarava and he gets rid of Gareth Delany. Delany pre-meditates and shimmies down the wicket. Ngarava pulls the length back and angles it across from around leg stump. Delany looks to slap it away but misses and the ball castles into the off pole. Ireland lose their ninth wicket now.
Back of a length and around off, this is dabbed away in front of covers for a single.
Nice change up! Takes pace off the ball and bowls it on a length over middle and leg. Gareth Delany misses the slog by a long way and the ball just goes over the stumps.
Excellent running again and these are crucial runs here for Ireland. Short and wide again, Gareth Delany mistimes the lofted drive through cover-point and hurries back for the second.
FOUR! Slapped away and the 100 is up for Ireland! This is banged in short and wide, Gareth Delany holds his shape and lofts it over wide mid off for a boundary.
Two more! Shorter and around leg stump, Delany works it off his hips and past the diving fielder at backward square leg for a brace.
Back of a length around middle and angling in. Gareth Delany hops and looks to work it leg side but gets a leading edge through cover-point for a couple of runs.
On middle and leg, flicked away to deep mid-wicket for one.
Excellent running! This is shorter and on leg stump, Gareth Delany works it to the left of square leg and races back for the second with ease.
Flights it up nicely outside off, Delany defends it out.
FOUR! Well struck! This is a half-volley outside off, Gareth Delany lofts it inside-out over extra cover and finds the fence.
This is fuller and down the leg side, Hand flicks it behind square and picks up a single.
On the shorter side and angling into the pads, Delany works it on the leg side for one.
FOUR! This is quicker and flatter around off, Fionn Hand chops it past short third man and the ball tirckles away into the fence.
Flighted delivery, a tad outside off. Gareth Delany drills it down to long on and sneaks a run.
This is shorter and sliding into middle, Gareth Delany keeps it out.
Flatter around off, this is nudged away toward backward point.

Just in! Fionn Hand survives! This is on middle and leg, Gareth Delany flicks it well in front of mid-wicket and looks for two straight away. Sean Williams in the deep picks it up and fires in a throw at the non-striker's end. The throw is a bit wide and Wellington Masakadza has to reach to collect the ball and whip off the bails. The replays show that this delay allowed Hand to drag his bat in.

Is that a run-out? Fionn Hand seems to be struggling here and Zimbabwe are confident. The third umpire is called in. He checks it from a lot of different angles and finds that Hand is just in. Not Out!
Nagging length on off stump, pushed back to the bowler.

EDGED AND FOUR! This is fuller and around off, turning away. Fionn Hand goes for the booming cover drive but gets a thick outside edge that flies past the man at first slip and runs away into the third man fence.
Fionn Hand walks in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Ireland are going down in a hurry here. Ryan Burl bowls it on a shorter length and turns it away from outside off. It is there to be cut and Mark Adair opts to do so off the back foot. The ball just sticks on the surface a bit and Adair ends up slicing it in front of short third man. Craig Ervine takes an easy catch diving forward and Zimbabwe are now two wickets away from bundling out the opposition.
Commentary.Howout: c Craig Ervine b Ryan Burl

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! This is quicker and shorter around off. Adair looks for the cut but the ball zips past the outside edge.
Flatter delivery on off, Mark Adair punches it off the back foot past point.
This is the googly, turning into the pads, Mark Adair picks it up and works it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
This is full and on off, driven through mid off for a single.

DROPPED! Oh, the bowler has made a mess of it! This is a tad shorter and drifted onto middle. The ball sticks in the surface and turns away. Mark Adair looks to flick but closes the face of the bat early and gets a leading edge. The ball pops up over the bowler's head who is slow to get to it and the stumps also come in between. In the end, Wellington only gets a fingertip on it.
Mark Adair is the new man in.

OUT! TAKEN! Straight to the man and Wellington Masakadza gets his second wicket of the over. This is simply poor batting from the Iriosh batters. This is bowled on a length around off and turning away. Tyrone Kane slogs it against the turn and takes on the longer part of the ground. This is hit flat and towards deep mid-wicket where Wesley Madhevere takes a simple catch around his face. Kane departs and Ireland are seven down inside the 14th over.
Commentary.Howout: c Wesley Madhevere b Wellington Masakadza

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up full and around middle, Delany pushes it to mid on for a quick single.
Flatter one again around off, Gareth Delany tentatively blocks it out.
Gareth Delany is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! A ripper of a take from Clive Madande behind the sticks and Curtis Campher has to depart. Campher backs away past the leg stump and Wellington Masakadza follows hi with a quicker delivery. This is bowled flatter and angled in. Campher looks to cut close from the body but gets an inside edge. Clive pouches it sharply and that too low and the finger is eventually raised.
Commentary.Howout: c Clive Madande b Wellington Masakadza

Commentary.Commentary: This is shorter and outside off, Curtis Campher rocks back and cuts it straight to point.
Short and wide, cut away into front of cover-point.
Shorter and around middle, tucked away through mid-wicket for a single.
And again but just for a single this time. Fuller and outside off, broomed away towards deep backward square leg for one.
FOUR! This is floated up outside off, Tyrone Kane fetches the ball and sweeps it behind square leg for a boundary.
Nicely played! This is floated up around off stump, Kane lofts it over wide mid off and picks up a couple of runs.
This is bowled around middle, Campher pushes it down to long on for a single.
Flatter one on off stump, this is blocked back to the bowler.
Quicker one, bowled fuller and outside off, Tyrone Kane doesn't play at it.
Beaten! This is tossed up a bit, full and outside off, turning further away. Tyrone Kane has a swipe across the line but misses.
This is shorter and around off, Curtis Campher sweeps it past square leg for a run.
This is fired in around off, Tyrone Kane shimmies down the track and strokes it through covers for a single.
Flatter delivery around off, this is cut away to point.
Another googly, on a length and turning in from outside off, this is pushed away square on the off side for one.
Tyrone Kane is the new man in.

OUT! TIMBER! Ryan Burl has the last laugh here and sends George Dockrell packing! Burl drags the length back and bowls it quicker around middle. Dockrell looks for the pull but it is the googly and this one keeps a bit low as well. Dockrell gets beaten all ends up and the ball crashes into the stumps. An unecessary shot this one and Ireland have lost half their side now.
SIX! BANG! This is tossed up right in the slot around middle. George Dockrell clears the front leg and whacks it right back over the bowler's head for the first maximum of the game.

Is that a dropped catch? According to the umpire, yes it is! This is quicker and flatter around off, Curtis Campher looks to sweep but might have got a glove on it. Clive Madande fumbles the catch and they scamper through for one.
Cheeky again! This is on a length around middle, Campher gets inside the line and scoops it toward short fine leg for a couple of runs.
FOUR! Skillful from Curtis Campher. This is full and outside off, Campher attempts the reverse sweep and nails it wide of the man at short third man for a boundary.
On off, defended out.
Bowls it down leg, Curtis Campher looks to flick it but the ball brushes his pads and rolls towards short fine leg for one.
Slightly shorter and on off, George Dockrell looks to punch it but gets an inside edge towards fine leg for one.
Outside off, this is played towards point for one.
This one lands down leg, Curtis Campher misses his flick and gets a rap on his pads.
Bowls it on middle, George Dockrell tucks it to mid-wicket for one.
Wellington Masakadza comes into the attack now.
A juicy full toss on off, Curtis Campher slaps it to sweeper cover for a brace.
Fuller ball on the off, Dockrell drives it to covers for a single.
This one lands outside off, George Dockrell looks to play at it but misses.
Fuller and on off, George Dockrell blocks it back.
George Dockrell walks in with Ireland in a spot of bother.

OUT! BOWLED! Here comes the wrong 'un and Tector gets completely deceived by it. This one lands on off, it turns in a bit, Harry Tector looks to loft it but misses it completely and the ball rattles over the leg pole. Harry Tector makes his way back into the pavilion.
Bowls it on off, Harry Tector eases it to short covers.

Fuller and on off, Curtis Campher drives it but finds the man at covers. The Zimbabwe players are asking for a catch and the umpires come together for a chat. The third umpire is called in and he checks it from a few different angles. This one seems to be really close but the benefit of the doubt might be given to the batter. The third umpire concludes that it is indeed a bump-ball.
Bowls it on off, Curtis Campher slaps it towards deep point for a brace.
Bowls it on off, this is defended towards point.
Fuller and on off, Harry Tector eases it to covers for one again.
This is floated up outside off, and Curtis Campher drives it behind square on the off side for a single.
Length ball on the off, Harry Tector cuts it to the point region for a single.
Sean Williams to roll his arm over.
Outside off this time, Curtis Campher eases it to the man at point.
Fuller and on off, this is defended out solidly.
FOUR! Similar to the last delivery, Curtis Campher looks to play at it but gets a thick outside edge as the ball races away to the third man fence for a boundary!
Bowls it outside off, turning away, Curtis Campher looks to play at it but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Fuller and on off, Harry Tector flicks it towards square leg for one.
Bowls it on leg, this is blocked back towards the bowler.
Curtis Campher is the new man in. Also, Ryan Burl has now been brought into the attack.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! A bit of swing and another one bites the dust. This one lands shorter and outside off, Stephen Doheny moves forward to slap it away through covers but misses it completely, gets the slightest of the edge and Clive Madande behind the sticks makes no mistake. Stephen Doheny makes his way back to the hut!
Commentary.Howout: c Clive Madande b Brad Evans

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on off, Stephen Doheny flicks it towards deep square leg for a brace.
This one lands down leg, Harry Tector looks to flick it but the ball brushes his pads and rolls towards short fine leg. They cross for a leg bye.
Bowls it outside off, Harry Tector looks to play at it but misses.
On a length and on off, Stephen Doheny flicks it towards square leg for one.
FOUR! Slightly shorter and on off, Stephen Doheny moves forward and slices it over point for a boundary!
On a length and on off, Stephen Doheny eases it to mid on for one.
FOUR! Fine shot. Shorter and on off, Stephen Doheny moves forward and carves it over backward point for a boundary!
Similar to the last delivery, Harry Tector steers it to covers for one.
Good-length delivery, angling in, Harry Tector eases it to covers.
This one lands outside off, Harry Tector looks to thrash it through covers but misses.
Bowls it on off, Harry Tector blocks it towards point.
Richard Ngarava (1-0-6-1) to bowl from the opposite end now.
This one lands down leg, Harry Tector tickles it towards short fine leg for one.
Fuller one this time, Stephen Doheny eases it to covers for one.
Bowls it on off, this is blocked towards covers.

Dropped! Back of a length and outside off, shaping away a touch, Stephen Doheny looks to block it but gets a thick outside edge as the ball carries towards the first slip. The fielder there, Craig Ervine makes a good attempt forward but drops it. Close!
Play and a miss. This one lands outside off, Stephen Doheny looks to slap it but misses.
Bowls it outside off, Stephen Doheny defends it to point.
Brad Evans comes into the attack now.
Bowls it on off, Harry Tector eases it to the man at point.
Fuller and on middle, Harry Tector defends it back towards the bowler.
Bowls it outside off, Harry Tector leaves it alone.
Harry Tector is the new man in.

OUT! TAKEN! The skipper departs. Shorter and wide outside off, Andy Balbirnie looks to slap it but mistimes it completely, finds Ryan Burl at backward point who reacts well and takes a fine catch around his chest. Andy Balbirnie departs for just five runs!
Commentary.Howout: c Ryan Burl b Tendai Chatara

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls it outside off, Andy Balbirnie looks to play at it but misses.
FOUR! Fine shot. Fuller and on off, Andy Balbirnie moves forward and drives it through extra covers for a boundary!
Around off, blocked out.
Length ball outside off, Stephen Doheny shuffles across and clips it to square leg to get off the mark with a couple of runs.
Stephen Doheny, the other debutant comes in at number 3.

OUT! TIMBER! Richard Ngarava draws the first blood. Pulls his length back a bit, and bowls it on off and middle, Ross Adair shimmies down the wicket to slap it but misses it completely. The ball clips the top of the bails and Ross Adair makes his way back into the hut cheaply on debut. Zimbabwe have an early breakthrough in the game.
Angling in from outside off, Ross Adair blocks it back.
FOUR! Pitched up, on middle and leg, Ross Adair uses the pace of the ball and tickles it through fine leg for a boundary!
Fuller and on off, Ross Adair guides it to the man at covers.
Richard Ngarava to operate from the other end.
A dot ball to end the first over. Good-length ball on the off stump, Andy Balbirnie covers the line of the ball and defends it solidly.
Bowls it on off, Andy Balbirnie eases it to the man at covers.
Fuller and on off, Ross Adair knocks it to long on for one and gets his first runs in international cricket.
Some extra bounce, on off, Ross Adair taps it to the man at point.
Outside off, Andy Balbirnie guides it to backward point for one.
On a length, some extra bounce, angling in, Andy Balbirnie looks to block it but gets an inside edge as the ball bounces off the deck.

Right then, we are done with the pre-match proceedings. Zimbabwe players are seen in a huddle, near the ropes. Ross Adair and Andy Balbirnie are the opening pair for Ireland. Tendai Chatara comes to bowl. Here we go...
We are all set for the game to begin. Both teams are lined up for the National anthem, It will be Ireland's first, followed by the National anthem of Zimbabwe.

Andy Balbirnie, the Irish skipper says that they were looking to bat first as they weren't sure and it is usually a good wicket here. Adds that they achieved their goal in the T20 World Cup but just like Zimbabwe, they too left a bit of something there and could have achieved more. Adds that Stephen and Ross Adair are all set to make their senior debuts. Ends by saying that in T20 cricket it doesn't matter much whether you bat first or second, you just have to do well.

Craig Ervine the skipper of Zimbabwe says that they will bowl first. Adds that it has a bit of moisture and they will look to restrict their opponents to a low total. Ends by saying that they will look forward to win this game. Confirms that Gary Ballance will make his debut for Zimbabwe in this game.
PITCH REPORT - The pitch should have a bit of swing and it has a bit of grass as well. The pitch is nice and hard and has some moisture in the air as well. The pitch supports the bowling side.

Ireland (Playing XI) - Andy Balbirnie (C), Harry Tector, Ross Adair (On debut), Curtis Campher, Gareth Delany, George Dockrell, Stephen Doheny (On debut) (WK), Fionn Hand, Tyrone Kane, Barry McCarthy and Mark Adair.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Tadiwanashe Marumani, Craig Ervine (C), Gary Ballance (On debut), Wesley Madhevere, Sean Williams, Ryan Burl, Clive Madande (WK), Brad Evans, Wellington Masakadza, Richard Ngarava and Tendai Chatara.
TOSS - Zimbabwe have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

Just like the hosts, Ireland will be also without key players such as Paul Stirling, Lorcan Tucker and Josh Little due to their professional commitments elsewhere. Andy Balbirnie will continue to lead the side and will be crucial if the visiting team is to win the series. Former English international, Gary Ballance might make his T20I debut here for his country of birth and the bowling attack will be led by Mark Adair. Can the hosts start off with a win? Or will Ireland spoil the party and take the lead? We shall find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit.

The hosts, Zimbabwe will be without their star all-rounder Sikandar Raza who is playing franchise cricket and their spearhead Blessing Muzarabani will not be a part of thisT20I series either. The attack will be led by Tendai Chatara while the experience of Craig Ervine and Sean Williams will matter a lot when it comes to the hosts' batting. Zimbabwe didn't have a great T20 World Cup a few months earlier but did defeat Pakistan and that win should give them a lot of confidence coming into this clash.

Hello and a warm welcome everyone to a brand new white-ball series between Zimbabwe and Ireland. The two nations are set to play each other in a three-game T20I series first, followed by a three-game ODI series as well. All six games will be played at the Harare Sports Club in Harare and both sides will look to start the series on a positive note.
... MATCH DAY ...

A brand new series is on the cards as Ireland have travelled to Zimbabwe for a 3-match T20I and ODI series. First up, it will be the shortest format that will be on display and as usual, all the action will be taking place in Harare. In the year of the 50-over World Cup, this may not hold much importance, but Ireland will take the upcoming three games to acclimatize to the conditions and also figure out their playing combination. It was a decent outing for these two teams in the recently concluded T20 World Cup although they could have done better given the potential they possess. The Irish team got the better of West Indies and England while Zimbabwe created a big upset by defeating Pakistan in a thriller. They will be aiming for improvement and getting even better from hereon. Regarding the two squads, they have quite a few new names but the core of the team has remained more or less unchanged, apart from a few notable absentees. Sikandar Raza, the man in the form of his life, has been granted permission to play franchise cricket while Blessing Muzarabani (injured), Regis Chakabva and Milton Shumba are other regulars not in the mix. Craig Ervine will continue to lead them and he will have the services of Sean Williams, Tendai Chatara, Ryan Burl and Richard Ngarava at his disposal who have been around for quite some time. The former English player, Gary Ballance has also been included in the Zimbabwean squad after he signed a 2-year deal with the country of his birth. He will definitely provide solidity to the batting group and his experience will be handy. Ireland, on the other hand, will also be without Paul Stirling, Josh Little and Lorcan Tucker who will also be busy playing franchise cricket and could join for the ODIs. Simi Singh has been dropped while Craig Young is sidelined with an injury. The Irish team management is taking this opportunity to test the quality of the fringe players. They look a shade lighter in the bowling department but have enough firepower in batting. This will be Ireland's first T20I game in Zimbabwe after their last tour in 2020 was cancelled due to the COVID-19 outbreak. Both teams are closely matched in skills, and we can expect a tight game.
